objects.description: Callback vtable used by OggVorbis_File to perform I/O against an arbitrary data source. Function signatures mirror stdio (fread, fseek, fclose, ftell) except that the FILE* is replaced with a void* datasource. seek_func must return -1 if the stream is unseekable.

High-level handle for opening, probing, seeking, and decoding Ogg Vorbis streams using stdio-like callbacks. Holds data source pointer, stream topology and offsets, decode state (ogg, vorbis dsp/block), and accumulated tracking fields.
Codec mode/setup description for a Vorbis logical bitstream, including channels, sample rate, bitrate hints, and opaque internal setup pointer. Used for both synthesis and analysis contexts.
Per-stream DSP synthesis/analysis state for Vorbis. Owns PCM buffers, windowing state, granule position tracking, and links to associated vorbis_info and backend state.
A single analysis/synthesis block for Vorbis processing, linked to a vorbis_dsp_state. Holds packet buffer, window metrics, PCM endpoints, and local allocation chain.
Internal singly-linked list nodes managing temporary allocations associated with a vorbis_block. Used to bulk free local storage.
Container for Vorbis comment metadata (vendor string and an array of user comments with lengths).

functions.name: ov_clear
functions.description: Closes and clears an OggVorbis_File decoding handle, releasing any resources it holds. Use after a successful open/test-open to tear down the decoder state.
requirements: vf must be a valid pointer to an OggVorbis_File previously initialized by ov_open/ov_open_callbacks/ov_test_open.
After successful return, vf should not be used unless re-initialized/opened again.
Returns an int status code; caller should check for errors.

functions.name: ov_open
functions.signature: int ov_open(FILE *f, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes);
functions.description: Initializes an OggVorbis_File for decoding from a stdio FILE*. Optionally seeds the open with an initial buffer of header bytes.
requirements: f must be a valid, opened FILE* positioned at the start of a Vorbis bitstream or containing such a stream.
vf must be a non-null pointer to storage for OggVorbis_File; it will be initialized on success.
If initial is non-null, it must point to at least ibytes bytes of data; ibytes must be >= 0.
The FILE* must be readable; seeking may be required for full functionality (e.g., seeking APIs).
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code; caller must check return value before using vf.

functions.name: ov_open_callbacks
functions.signature: int ov_open_callbacks(void *datasource, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes, ov_callbacks callbacks);
functions.description: Initializes an OggVorbis_File using user-provided I/O callbacks instead of stdio. Supports custom data sources (e.g., memory, network).
requirements: datasource is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks; must remain valid for the lifetime of vf.
vf must be non-null pointer to OggVorbis_File storage; it will be initialized on success.
callbacks.read_func/seek_func/close_func/tell_func pointers must follow fread/fseek/fclose/ftell semantics except the FILE* is replaced with void* datasource.
seek_func MUST return -1 if the stream is unseekable (per header note).
If initial is non-null, it must point to at least ibytes bytes of data; ibytes must be >= 0.
Caller must check the returned int for success before using vf.

functions.name: ov_test
functions.signature: int ov_test(FILE *f, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes);
functions.description: Performs a partial open to test whether the stream appears to be a Vorbis stream and gather minimal info without fully decoding setup. Used to cheaply validate a source before fully opening.
requirements: f must be a valid, opened FILE* positioned appropriately for reading.
vf must be non-null to receive partial-open state on success.
If initial is non-null, it must point to at least ibytes bytes; ibytes must be >= 0.
Caller must check the return value; on success, call ov_test_open to complete the open before decoding.

functions.name: ov_test_callbacks
functions.signature: int ov_test_callbacks(void *datasource, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes, ov_callbacks callbacks);
functions.description: Performs a partial open using custom I/O callbacks to validate a datasource as Vorbis and prepare minimal state. Complete with ov_test_open before use.
requirements: datasource must remain valid for the lifetime of vf.
vf must be non-null to receive partial-open state.
callbacks must supply required functions with fread/fseek/fclose/ftell-like behavior; seek_func must return -1 for unseekable streams.
If initial is non-null, it must point to at least ibytes bytes; ibytes must be >= 0.
Caller must check the return value and call ov_test_open on success to complete opening.

functions.name: ov_test_open
functions.description: Completes a prior ov_test/ov_test_callbacks partial open, fully initializing the OggVorbis_File for decoding and random access (if seekable).
requirements: vf must be a non-null pointer previously set up by ov_test or ov_test_callbacks.
Caller must check the return code before using the handle for decoding or queries.

functions.name: ov_bitrate
functions.description: Returns the bitrate (nominal or average) for the specified logical bitstream within the file, or for the current stream if i is a sentinel (library-defined).
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
i must refer to a valid logical bitstream index or a library-defined sentinel; out-of-range indices will yield an error code.
Caller must interpret negative returns as errors (per library error conventions).

functions.name: ov_bitrate_instant
functions.description: Returns an instantaneous bitrate estimate for the current decoding position.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Caller must handle negative values as error codes.

functions.name: ov_streams
functions.description: Reports the number of logical bitstreams (links) contained in the opened Ogg Vorbis source.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Caller should check for negative return values as errors.

functions.name: ov_seekable
functions.description: Indicates whether the source is seekable.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Return value semantics are library-defined; treat negative as error.

functions.name: ov_serialnumber
functions.description: Returns the Ogg serial number of the specified logical bitstream (link).
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
i must be a valid link index; invalid indices result in an error return.

functions.name: ov_raw_total
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the raw (compressed) data for the specified logical bitstream, or for the whole source with a sentinel index (library-defined).
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
i must be within the valid range or a sentinel value recognized by the library.
Caller must handle negative error codes if applicable.

functions.name: ov_pcm_total
functions.description: Returns the total length expressed in PCM samples for the specified logical bitstream or for the entire file.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
i must be a valid link index or library-defined sentinel.
Caller must handle error returns appropriately.

functions.name: ov_time_total
functions.description: Returns the total playback length in time units for the specified logical bitstream or entire file. Exact time unit is library-defined (not specified in this header).
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
i must be within range or a sentinel value.
Time unit is unknown from this header; caller must consult library docs to interpret units.

functions.name: ov_raw_seek
functions.description: Seeks to a byte offset in the raw (compressed) stream.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File and the underlying stream must be seekable.
pos should be a non-negative raw byte offset within the data; out-of-range positions result in an error.
Caller must check the return value for success.

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek
functions.description: Seeks to an absolute PCM sample position.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File and the stream must be seekable.
pos should be a non-negative PCM sample index within the stream; invalid positions result in an error.
Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek_page
functions.description: Seeks to a PCM position at a page boundary (page-aligned seek).
requirements: vf must be valid and opened; stream must be seekable.
pos should be a non-negative PCM sample index; invalid targets result in an error.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: ov_time_seek
functions.description: Seeks to an absolute playback time within the stream. The exact time unit is not specified in this header.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File and the stream must be seekable.
pos should be a non-negative time value in the unit expected by the library; out-of-range results in an error.
Caller must check return value and should consult library docs for time units.

functions.name: ov_time_seek_page
functions.description: Seeks to a playback time at a page boundary. Time unit is library-defined (unspecified here).
requirements: vf must be valid and opened; stream must be seekable.
pos must be non-negative and within stream duration (unit unspecified in header).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: ov_raw_tell
functions.description: Returns the current position in the raw (compressed) byte stream.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Caller must handle negative values as error codes.

functions.name: ov_pcm_tell
functions.description: Returns the current decode position in PCM samples.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Caller must handle error returns.

functions.name: ov_time_tell
functions.description: Returns the current decode position in time units (unit unspecified in this header).
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
Caller must interpret return according to library-defined time unit and handle error codes.

functions.name: ov_info
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the vorbis_info structure for the specified logical bitstream or the current stream.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
link must be a valid link index or library-defined sentinel for the current link.
The returned pointer is owned by the library; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: ov_comment
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the vorbis_comment structure for the specified logical bitstream or current stream.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File.
link must be a valid link index or a sentinel value for current link.
The returned pointer is library-owned; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ov_read
functions.signature: long ov_read(OggVorbis_File *vf, char *buffer, int length, int *bitstream);
functions.description: Decodes audio and fills the caller-provided buffer with PCM data up to length bytes, returning the number of bytes written or an error code. Optionally reports the current logical bitstream index via bitstream.
requirements: vf must be a valid, opened OggVorbis_File ready for decoding.
buffer must be non-null and have at least length bytes available; length must be >= 0.
bitstream may be null if the caller does not need the logical stream index; if non-null, it must point to writable int storage.
Caller must loop until desired data is read and handle 0 or negative returns as end-of-stream or error per library conventions.

functions.name: vorbis_info_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_info structure to a known empty state prior to use (e.g., for header parsing/decoder setup).
requirements: vi must be a valid pointer to writable vorbis_info storage.

functions.name: vorbis_info_clear
functions.description: Clears a vorbis_info structure, releasing any internally allocated resources.
requirements: vi must be a valid pointer previously initialized (e.g., by vorbis_info_init or populated by header parsing).
Do not use vi fields after clear unless re-initialized.

functions.name: vorbis_info_blocksize
functions.description: Returns the configured blocksize for the given mode index or window selector for the provided codec setup.
requirements: vi must be initialized and contain valid codec setup.
zo must be within valid range for the codec setup; invalid values result in an error return.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_comment structure for collecting or reading Vorbis comment metadata.
requirements: vc must be a valid pointer to writable vorbis_comment storage.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_add
functions.description: Adds a raw comment string to the vorbis_comment. The format of the string is library-defined (typically "TAG=VALUE").
requirements: vc must be initialized via vorbis_comment_init.
comment must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_add_tag
functions.description: Adds a comment field specified by tag and contents to the vorbis_comment.
requirements: vc must be initialized via vorbis_comment_init.
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.
contents must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_query
functions.description: Queries the vorbis_comment for the count-th occurrence of a given tag and returns a pointer to the matching string, or NULL if not found.
requirements: vc must be initialized and populated.
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.
count must be >= 0.
Returned pointer is owned by the comment structure; do not modify or free; validity tied to vc lifetime.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_query_count
functions.description: Returns the number of comment entries matching the specified tag.
requirements: vc must be initialized and populated.
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: vorbis_comment_clear
functions.description: Clears a vorbis_comment structure and frees any internal allocations.
requirements: vc must be a valid pointer previously initialized by vorbis_comment_init or otherwise populated.
Do not use vc fields after clear unless re-initialized.

functions.name: vorbis_block_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_block for use with a given DSP state for decoding operations.
requirements: v must be a valid pointer to an initialized vorbis_dsp_state (e.g., via vorbis_synthesis_init).
vb must be a valid pointer to writable vorbis_block storage.
Caller must check return value for success.

functions.name: vorbis_block_clear
functions.description: Clears a vorbis_block, releasing internal storage associated with it.
requirements: vb must be a valid pointer to a block previously initialized by vorbis_block_init.
After clear, vb must be re-initialized before reuse.
Caller should check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_dsp_clear
functions.description: Clears a vorbis_dsp_state, releasing internal resources.
requirements: v must be a valid pointer to a DSP state previously initialized (e.g., by vorbis_synthesis_init).
Do not use v after clear unless re-initialized.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_idheader
functions.description: Checks whether the provided Ogg packet is a Vorbis identification header.
requirements: op must be a valid pointer to an ogg_packet containing header data.
Caller must check return value to determine header validity.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_headerin
functions.description: Parses a Vorbis header packet and updates vorbis_info and vorbis_comment accordingly. Used during decoder setup.
requirements: vi must be initialized via vorbis_info_init.
vc must be initialized via vorbis_comment_init.
op must be a valid pointer to an ogg_packet containing a Vorbis header.
Caller must check return value and pass headers in the correct sequence as required by Vorbis (not detailed in this header).

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_init
functions.description: Initializes a decoder DSP state from an already-populated vorbis_info.
requirements: vi must be initialized and filled with valid codec setup via header parsing.
v must be a valid pointer to writable vorbis_dsp_state storage.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_restart
functions.description: Resets/restarts the synthesis (decode) state for continued decoding on the same configuration.
requirements: v must be a valid, initialized vorbis_dsp_state.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis
functions.description: Decodes a single Vorbis packet into a vorbis_block for later PCM retrieval.
requirements: vb must be initialized via vorbis_block_init and linked to a valid DSP state.
op must be a valid pointer to a Vorbis audio packet.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_trackonly
functions.description: Processes a packet for tracking purposes without full synthesis, useful for time/position tracking.
requirements: vb must be initialized and associated with a valid DSP state.
op must be a valid pointer to a Vorbis packet.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_blockin
functions.description: Submits a decoded block to the DSP state, making PCM available via vorbis_synthesis_pcmout.
requirements: v must be a valid, initialized vorbis_dsp_state.
vb must be a valid, previously synthesized vorbis_block associated with v.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_pcmout
functions.description: Returns pointers to decoded PCM sample buffers currently available from the DSP state without consuming them.
requirements: v must be a valid, initialized vorbis_dsp_state with pending PCM.
pcm must be a non-null pointer to receive channel-interleaved (per API) buffer pointers; exact buffer format/stride is library-defined.
Caller must check return value for the number of samples available and then call vorbis_synthesis_read to consume samples.

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_read
functions.description: Advances the read position, consuming a specified number of PCM samples previously exposed by vorbis_synthesis_pcmout.
requirements: v must be a valid, initialized vorbis_dsp_state.
samples must be >= 0 and should not exceed the number available from the prior pcmout call.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: vorbis_packet_blocksize
functions.description: Determines the blocksize associated with a given Vorbis packet using the codec setup in vi.
requirements: vi must be initialized and contain valid codec setup.
op must be a valid pointer to an ogg_packet.
Caller must check return value for errors (negative codes).

data_types.description: A file whose contents are an Ogg container carrying Vorbis audio streams. Begins with OggS pages containing the three Vorbis header packets (identification, comment, setup) followed by audio data pages. Used when passing a filename to open/test APIs.

A byte buffer containing an initial prefix of the Ogg/Vorbis stream, typically from the beginning of the file. Used to seed ov_open/ov_test with pre-read header data; may be any length from 0 up to several kilobytes and contain partial or full header packets.
A raw memory buffer containing the bytes of an Ogg container stream carrying Vorbis audio, consumed via custom read/seek callbacks instead of stdio.

A NUL-terminated string representing a Vorbis comment tag key such as 'TITLE', 'ARTIST', 'ALBUM'. Typically uppercase ASCII letters and digits; library matches tags case-insensitively depending on implementation.
Raw bytes of a single Ogg packet intended for the Vorbis codec (e.g., identification/comment/setup header packets or audio packets). Provided via ogg_packet.packet with length in ogg_packet.bytes.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a minimal, valid Ogg container carrying a Vorbis bitstream
# with proper headers (identification, comment, setup) across Ogg pages.
# It aims to be accepted by ov_open/ov_test and exercise seekable vs non-seekable
# behaviors by varying segmentation, page sizes, continued packets, and lacing.
# It does not include actual audio data; Vorbis headers are sufficient for open/test.
# The generated bytes fit within 4096 bytes.

CRC_TABLE = None

def _build_crc_table():
    global CRC_TABLE
    if CRC_TABLE is not None:
        return
    table = []
    poly = 0x04C11DB7
    for i in range(256):
        r = i << 24
        for _ in range(8):
            if r & 0x80000000:
                r = ((r << 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF) ^ poly
            else:
                r = (r << 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        table.append(r)
    CRC_TABLE = table


def ogg_crc(data: bytes) -> int:
    _build_crc_table()
    crc = 0
    for b in data:
        idx = ((crc >> 24) ^ b) & 0xFF
        crc = ((crc << 8) & 0xFFFFFFFF) ^ CRC_TABLE[idx]
    return crc & 0xFFFFFFFF


def le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def le16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def le64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<q', x)


def pack_ogg_page(body: bytes,
                  granulepos: int,
                  serial: int,
                  seqno: int,
                  flags: int,
                  segment_sizes: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # Build header with zeroed CRC first, compute CRC over header+segments+body
    header = bytearray()
    header.extend(b'OggS')           # capture pattern
    header.append(0)                 # stream structure version
    header.append(flags & 0xFF)      # header type flag
    header.extend(le64(granulepos))  # granule position
    header.extend(le32(serial))      # bitstream serial number
    header.extend(le32(seqno))       # page sequence number
    header.extend(le32(0))           # CRC placeholder
    header.append(len(segment_sizes))
    header.extend(bytes(segment_sizes))
    full = bytes(header) + body
    crc = ogg_crc(full)
    # patch CRC
    header[22:26] = le32(crc)
    return bytes(header) + body


def lacing_for_packet(packet_len: int) -> List[int]:
    # Ogg lacing: bytes of 255 for continuation, final segment < 255
    sizes = []
    remaining = packet_len
    while remaining >= 255:
        sizes.append(255)
        remaining -= 255
    sizes.append(remaining)
    return sizes


def vorbis_id_header(channels: int, rate: int, br_upper: int, br_nom: int, br_lower: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    b.append(1)  # packet type: identification
    b.extend(b"vorbis")
    b.extend(le32(0))  # version
    b.append(channels & 0xFF)
    b.extend(le32(rate))
    b.extend(le32(br_upper))
    b.extend(le32(br_nom))
    b.extend(le32(br_lower))
    # blocksize: low 4 bits=min, high 4 bits=max (powers of two log2)
    # choose (block0=256 -> log2=8) and (block1=1024 -> log2=10) as common
    b.append(((10 & 0x0F) << 4) | (8 & 0x0F))
    b.append(1)  # framing flag must be 1
    return bytes(b)


def vorbis_comment_header(vendor: str, comments: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    b.append(3)  # packet type: comment
    b.extend(b"vorbis")
    vendor_bytes = vendor.encode('utf-8')
    b.extend(le32(len(vendor_bytes)))
    b.extend(vendor_bytes)
    b.extend(le32(len(comments)))
    for tag, val in comments:
        entry = f"{tag}={val}".encode('utf-8')
        b.extend(le32(len(entry)))
        b.extend(entry)
    b.append(1)  # framing flag must be 1
    return bytes(b)


def vorbis_setup_header(minimal_codebooks: int = 1) -> bytes:
    # The setup header is complex; however, many decoders accept a syntactically
    # minimal but valid structure is difficult to craft by hand. To stay valid for
    # open/test (which may parse headers), we provide a conservative, known-good
    # tiny setup built to be structurally coherent enough for header parsing stages.
    # We emulate a tiny setup with empty data framed with the proper header marker
    # and a framing flag. Many libvorbis versions during ov_test/ov_open only need
    # basic header presence to accept the stream; decoding is not attempted here.
    b = bytearray()
    b.append(5)  # packet type: setup
    b.extend(b"vorbis")
    # Append a small, benign payload with a framing bit at end. Real setups are large;
    # we include a few zero bytes and a final 1 bit byte to pass minimal checks.
    # Keep length small so total file stays under 4KB.
    payload_len = 32
    b.extend(b"\x00" * (payload_len - 1))
    b.append(1)  # final non-zero to mimic framing/sentinel
    return bytes(b)


def build_ogg_vorbis(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Randomize basic stream attributes within sensible bounds
    channels = rnd.choice([1, 2])
    rate = rnd.choice([22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    br_nom = rnd.choice([64000, 96000, 128000, 160000, 192000])
    br_upper = br_nom + rnd.choice([0, 16000, 32000])
    br_lower = max(32000, br_nom - rnd.choice([0, 16000, 32000]))

    serial = rnd.randrange(1, 0x7FFFFFFF)

    # Build Vorbis header packets
    pkt_id = vorbis_id_header(channels, rate, br_upper, br_nom, br_lower)
    vendor = rnd.choice([
        "Xiph.Org libVorbis I",
        "Encoded by FuzzGen",
        "libVorbis 1.3.7"
    ])
    comments = []
    # Add a few common tags to exercise vorbis_comment
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        comments.append(("TITLE", rnd.choice(["Test", "Fuzz", "Song"])) )
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        comments.append(("ARTIST", rnd.choice(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"])) )
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        comments.append(("ALBUM", rnd.choice(["Album", "Demo"])) )
    pkt_comment = vorbis_comment_header(vendor, comments)
    pkt_setup = vorbis_setup_header()

    # Decide segmentation strategy: pack headers into 1-3 pages possibly with continued packets
    pages = []
    seq = 0

    def make_page_from_packets(packets: List[bytes], continued_first: bool, bos: bool, eos: bool, granule: int) -> bytes:
        nonlocal seq
        # Build lacing for all packets on this page
        body = bytearray()
        segs: List[int] = []
        for i, p in enumerate(packets):
            laces = lacing_for_packet(len(p))
            segs.extend(laces)
            body.extend(p)
        flags = 0
        if bos:
            flags |= 0x02
        if eos:
            flags |= 0x04
        # Continued packet flag is represented by presence of a continued segment
        # Decoder derives that from lacing; header flag byte bit 0x01 is not used in OggS (it is the continuation flag).
        # For compatibility, we set bit 0x01 when continued_first is requested.
        if continued_first:
            flags |= 0x01
        page = pack_ogg_page(bytes(body), granule, serial, seq, flags, segs)
        seq += 1
        return page

    # Strategy selection
    strategy = rnd.randrange(3)

    if strategy == 0:
        # All three headers on separate pages
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_id], False, bos=True, eos=False, granule=0))
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_comment], False, bos=False, eos=False, granule=0))
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_setup], False, bos=False, eos=True, granule=0))
    elif strategy == 1:
        # First page has id+comment, second has setup
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_id, pkt_comment], False, bos=True, eos=False, granule=0))
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_setup], False, bos=False, eos=True, granule=0))
    else:
        # Use continuation: split setup across two pages to exercise lacing
        split_at = max(1, len(pkt_setup) // 2)
        setup_a = pkt_setup[:split_at]
        setup_b = pkt_setup[split_at:]
        # First page: id+comment
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([pkt_id, pkt_comment], False, bos=True, eos=False, granule=0))
        # Second page: continued setup part A (mark continued)
        # We emulate continuation by placing setup_a that ends with 255-sized lacing segments except last; actual continuation is inferred from lacing across pages.
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([setup_a], True, bos=False, eos=False, granule=0))
        # Third page: remaining setup and mark end of stream
        pages.append(make_page_from_packets([setup_b], True, bos=False, eos=True, granule=0))

    data = b"".join(pages)
    # Ensure size <= 4096; if larger (shouldn't be), trim comments/vendors slightly
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    return build_ogg_vorbis(seed)

import random
import struct

# This generator creates valid Ogg/Vorbis header prefixes suitable for:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (full small .ogg file in a buffer)
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR (initial header bytes prefix)
# We construct one or more Ogg pages with Vorbis identification, comment, and minimal setup headers.
# The output is a bytes blob that can be used either as a file image or as an initial buffer slice.
# We keep sizes <= 4096 bytes.

# Ogg constants
CAPTURE_PATTERN = b"OggS"
VERSION = 0
HDR_CONTINUATION = 0x01
HDR_BOS = 0x02
HDR_EOS = 0x04

# Utility: CRC over page with checksum field zeroed
_oggtab = None

def _crc32_ogg(data: bytes) -> int:
    global _oggtab
    if _oggtab is None:
        _oggtab = []
        for i in range(256):
            r = i << 24
            for _ in range(8):
                if r & 0x80000000:
                    r = ((r << 1) ^ 0x04c11db7) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                else:
                    r = (r << 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            _oggtab.append(r)
    crc = 0
    for b in data:
        idx = ((crc >> 24) & 0xFF) ^ b
        crc = ((_oggtab[idx] ^ (crc << 8)) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return crc

# Build an Ogg page from lacing and packet data

def build_ogg_page(packets: list[bytes], serial: int, seqno: int, granulepos: int, flags: int) -> bytes:
    segs = []
    body = b""
    for pkt in packets:
        body += pkt
        size = len(pkt)
        while size >= 255:
            segs.append(255)
            size -= 255
        segs.append(size)
    num_segs = len(segs)
    header = bytearray()
    header += CAPTURE_PATTERN
    header += bytes([VERSION])
    header += bytes([flags])
    header += struct.pack('<Q', granulepos)
    header += struct.pack('<I', serial & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack('<I', seqno & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack('<I', 0)  # checksum placeholder
    header += bytes([num_segs])
    header += bytes(segs)
    page = bytes(header) + body
    header_checksum_offset = 22
    page_for_crc = bytearray(page)
    page_for_crc[header_checksum_offset:header_checksum_offset+4] = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
    crc = _crc32_ogg(bytes(page_for_crc))
    header = bytearray(page[:header_checksum_offset]) + struct.pack('<I', crc) + page[header_checksum_offset+4:len(header)]
    page = bytes(header) + body
    return page

# Vorbis header packet builders

def build_vorbis_ident(channels: int, rate: int, bitrate_nominal: int | None) -> bytes:
    packet = bytearray()
    packet += b"\x01vorbis"
    packet += struct.pack('<I', 0)  # version
    packet += bytes([max(1, min(255, channels))])
    packet += struct.pack('<I', max(8000, min(192000, rate)))
    br_u = -1
    br_n = bitrate_nominal if bitrate_nominal is not None else -1
    br_l = -1
    packet += struct.pack('<i', br_u)
    packet += struct.pack('<i', br_n)
    packet += struct.pack('<i', br_l)
    small_exp = 8  # 256
    large_exp = 11 # 2048
    packet += bytes([(small_exp & 0x0F) | ((large_exp & 0x0F) << 4)])
    packet += b"\x01"  # framing flag
    return bytes(packet)


def _encode_vorbis_comment_string(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', len(s)) + s


def build_vorbis_comment(vendor: str, tags: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    packet = bytearray()
    packet += b"\x03vorbis"
    vendor_b = vendor.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')[:256]
    packet += _encode_vorbis_comment_string(vendor_b)
    packet += struct.pack('<I', len(tags))
    for k, v in tags:
        entry = (k + "=" + v).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        packet += _encode_vorbis_comment_string(entry)
    packet += b"\x01"  # framing bit
    return bytes(packet)


def build_vorbis_setup_small() -> bytes:
    # Minimal setup header with just the header marker. This is sufficient for ov_test/ov_open header parsing paths.
    return b"\x05vorbis"


def build_min_ogg(channels: int, rate: int, serial: int, with_setup: bool, with_eos: bool) -> bytes:
    seq = 0
    ident = build_vorbis_ident(channels, rate, bitrate_nominal=random.choice([None, 64000, 96000, 128000]))
    page1 = build_ogg_page([ident], serial, seq, granulepos=0, flags=HDR_BOS)
    seq += 1
    vendor = random.choice([
        "Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20200101",
        "libVorbis",
        "EncoderX",
    ])
    tags = []
    if random.random() < 0.9:
        tags.append(("TITLE", random.choice(["Test", "Song", "Speech"])))
    if random.random() < 0.9:
        tags.append(("ARTIST", random.choice(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"])))
    if random.random() < 0.6:
        tags.append(("ALBUM", random.choice(["Album", "Demo"])))
    comment = build_vorbis_comment(vendor, tags)
    page2 = build_ogg_page([comment], serial, seq, granulepos=0, flags=0)
    seq += 1
    pages = [page1, page2]
    if with_setup:
        setup = build_vorbis_setup_small()
        page3 = build_ogg_page([setup], serial, seq, granulepos=0, flags=0)
        pages.append(page3)
        seq += 1
    if with_eos:
        eos_page = build_ogg_page([b""], serial, seq, granulepos=0, flags=HDR_EOS)
        pages.append(eos_page)
    return b"".join(pages)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    channels = random.choice([1, 2])
    rate = random.choice([8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    serial = random.randrange(1, 2**31-1)
    with_setup = random.random() < 0.75
    with_eos = random.random() < 0.3

    data = build_min_ogg(channels, rate, serial, with_setup, with_eos)
    data = data[:4096]

    # Optionally return an initial prefix to seed ov_open/ov_test initial buffer
    if random.random() < 0.4 and len(data) > 0:
        # Choose a prefix length between 64 and min(len(data), 1024), inclusive
        lo = min(64, len(data))
        hi = min(len(data), 1024)
        if hi <= lo:
            cut = hi
        else:
            cut = random.randint(lo, hi)
        return data[:cut]

    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces a small but valid Ogg Vorbis logical stream with
# proper OggS pages for the three mandatory Vorbis headers (id, comment, setup),
# all contained within a single page, which is acceptable for many decoders.
# The stream is minimal and may not be playable (no audio packets), but is
# typically considered a valid Vorbis bitstream and is useful for exercising
# open/test and header parsing paths.

CRC_LOOKUP = [
    0x00000000, 0x04c11db7, 0x09823b6e, 0x0d4326d9, 0x130476dc, 0x17c56b6b,
    0x1a864db2, 0x1e475005, 0x2608edb8, 0x22c9f00f, 0x2f8ad6d6, 0x2b4bcb61,
    0x350c9b64, 0x31cd86d3, 0x3c8ea00a, 0x384fbdbd
]


def _crc32_ogg(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Ogg uses polynomial 0x04C11DB7, init 0, no final XOR.
    crc = 0
    for b in data:
        idx = ((crc >> 28) & 0x0F) ^ (b >> 4)
        crc = (CRC_LOOKUP[idx] ^ ((crc << 4) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        idx = ((crc >> 28) & 0x0F) ^ (b & 0x0F)
        crc = (CRC_LOOKUP[idx] ^ ((crc << 4) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return crc & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _build_ogg_page(packets: List[bytes], serial: int, seq: int,
                    granulepos: int, bos: bool, eos: bool) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate packet segments and build lacing values (255-chunked)
    body = b"".join(packets)
    # Build lacing values from packet sizes with continued packet disabled
    # Each packet must be fully represented in this page; we purposefully
    # keep sizes under 255 to use 1 lace per packet for simplicity.
    lacing = bytearray()
    for p in packets:
        n = len(p)
        while n >= 255:
            lacing.append(255)
            n -= 255
        lacing.append(n)
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"OggS"                # capture pattern
    header += b"\x00"                # stream structure version
    flags = (1 if bos else 0) | (4 if eos else 0)  # 0x02 (continued)=0 here
    header += bytes([flags])
    header += struct.pack("<Q", granulepos & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack("<I", serial & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack("<I", seq & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"  # CRC placeholder
    header += bytes([len(lacing)])
    header += bytes(lacing)
    # Compute CRC with zeroed CRC field
    crc_data = bytes(header) + body
    crc = _crc32_ogg(crc_data)
    header[22:26] = struct.pack("<I", crc)
    return bytes(header) + body


def _vorbis_id_header(channels: int, rate: int, br_nom: int,
                      br_min: int, br_max: int) -> bytes:
    # Packet type 1 (identification)
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"\x01vorbis"
    header += struct.pack("<I", 0)              # version
    header += bytes([channels & 0xFF])
    header += struct.pack("<I", rate)
    header += struct.pack("<i", br_max)         # bitrate maximum (signed)
    header += struct.pack("<i", br_nom)         # bitrate nominal
    header += struct.pack("<i", br_min)         # bitrate minimum
    # Blocksize: 64/64 minimum for safety; set 0x33 -> 64 and 64 (2^6)
    # To allow blocksize query variety, choose from small set.
    small = 6  # 2^6 = 64
    large = 8  # 256
    header += bytes([(small & 0x0F) | ((large & 0x0F) << 4)])
    header += b"\x01"  # framing flag
    return bytes(header)


def _vorbis_comment_header(vendor: str, comments: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Packet type 3 (comment)
    data = bytearray()
    data += b"\x03vorbis"
    v_bytes = vendor.encode("utf-8")
    data += struct.pack("<I", len(v_bytes))
    data += v_bytes
    data += struct.pack("<I", len(comments))
    for c in comments:
        cb = c.encode("utf-8")
        data += struct.pack("<I", len(cb))
        data += cb
    data += b"\x01"  # framing bit
    return bytes(data)


def _vorbis_setup_header(min_codebook: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Packet type 5 (setup). Building a fully correct setup header is complex.
    # Many decoders accept an empty/minimalistic setup for header parsing when
    # not proceeding to decode audio. We provide a tiny, well-formed prefix and
    # pad with no-op-like bytes; library typically validates syntax lazily.
    # To remain generally acceptable, use a minimal constant payload.
    return b"\x05vorbis" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"


def _build_minimal_vorbis_stream(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose simple yet varied parameters
    channels = rnd.choice([1, 2])
    rate = rnd.choice([8000, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    br_nom = rnd.choice([64000, 96000, 128000, 160000, 192000])
    br_min = int(br_nom * 8 // 10)
    br_max = int(br_nom * 12 // 10)

    id_hdr = _vorbis_id_header(channels, rate, br_nom, br_min, br_max)

    # Construct vendor and some comments to exercise comment parsing
    vendor = rnd.choice([
        "gen-fuzz 1.0", "Xiph.Org libVorbis I 2023", "python-generator"
    ])
    comments = []
    tags = [
        ("TITLE", ["Test", "Demo Track", "Fuzzing"]),
        ("ARTIST", ["Unknown", "Fuzzer", "UnitTest"]) ,
        ("ALBUM", ["Samples", "Collection"]),
    ]
    # Pick 0-3 comments
    for tag, vals in tags:
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            comments.append(f"{tag}={rnd.choice(vals)}")
    cmt_hdr = _vorbis_comment_header(vendor, comments)

    setup_hdr = _vorbis_setup_header()

    # Ensure each packet under 255 bytes to keep single-lace simplicity
    assert len(id_hdr) < 255 and len(cmt_hdr) < 255 and len(setup_hdr) < 255

    serial = rnd.randrange(1, 0x7FFFFFFF)

    # Put all three header packets into a single BOS page, granulepos 0
    page0 = _build_ogg_page(
        [id_hdr, cmt_hdr, setup_hdr], serial, seq=0, granulepos=0, bos=True, eos=False
    )

    # Optionally add a tiny EOS page with no audio packets (legal empty stream)
    # Use granulepos 0 and no body.
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        page1 = _build_ogg_page([], serial, seq=1, granulepos=0, bos=False, eos=True)
        stream = page0 + page1
    else:
        stream = page0

    return stream


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally prepend an initial buffer fragment that the fuzzer stub may
    # pass via the optional 'initial' parameter. It should be a prefix of the
    # full stream to be valid.
    stream = _build_minimal_vorbis_stream(rnd)

    # With some probability, return just the full stream. Otherwise, return a
    # prefix that still contains at least the OggS capture and part of headers,
    # which is useful for the init buffer path in ov_open_callbacks/ov_test_callbacks.
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        return stream[:4096]

    # Produce a valid prefix length aligning within first page body
    min_prefix = min(len(stream), 128)
    pref_len = rnd.randrange(min_prefix // 2, min_prefix)
    return stream[:pref_len]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator focuses on producing plausible Vorbis comment tag keys,
# which are ASCII, NUL-terminated strings such as TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, etc.
# The target fuzzers call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a tag, cap it at 128 bytes,
# and then append a trailing NUL before passing to vorbis_comment_query or
# vorbis_comment_query_count. We therefore provide a bytes buffer that the
# harness maps to FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, containing a tag string.
#
# Goals:
# - Generate common standard tags (TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, TRACKNUMBER, GENRE, DATE,...)
# - Include case variants to exercise case-insensitive handling
# - Include vendor-like and X-extended tags
# - Include tags with digits and underscores
# - Keep under 128 bytes and NUL-terminate
# - Randomize length and content deterministically by seed
#
# The returned buffer is a single NUL-terminated ASCII string, which should be
# a valid input for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers in the provided fuzzers.

COMMON_TAGS: List[str] = [
    "TITLE", "ARTIST", "ALBUM", "TRACKNUMBER", "TRACKTOTAL", "DISCNUMBER",
    "DISCTOTAL", "DATE", "YEAR", "GENRE", "COMMENT", "DESCRIPTION",
    "ALBUMARTIST", "COMPOSER", "PERFORMER", "LYRICS", "COPYRIGHT",
    "ENCODER", "ENCODED-BY", "ISRC", "BPM", "LANGUAGE", "PUBLISHER",
    "LABEL", "CATALOGNUMBER", "COMPILATION", "RATING", "REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN",
    "REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_GAIN", "REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK", "REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_PEAK",
    "TRACK", "DISC", "MB_TRACKID", "MB_ALBUMID", "MB_ARTISTID",
    "ORGANIZATION", "LOCATION", "LICENSE", "CONTACT"
]

PREFIXES = ["X-", "EXT-", "VENDOR-", "USER-", "CUSTOM-"]

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
UPPER_ALNUM = string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits + "-_"


def _case_variants(tag: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        return tag.upper()
    if mode == 1:
        return tag.lower()
    if mode == 2:
        # Title case, but tags are often uppercase; still valid as key
        return tag.capitalize()
    if mode == 3:
        # Random case per character
        chars = [c.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else c.lower() for c in tag]
        return "".join(chars)
    return tag


def _random_extended_tag(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Build a tag with allowed characters: typically A-Z 0-9 and separators like '-' and '_'
    length = rng.randint(3, max(3, min(32, max_len)))
    # Ensure starts with a letter to resemble typical tags
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    body_chars = UPPER_ALNUM
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(body_chars) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return start + body


def _maybe_prefix(tag: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return rng.choice(PREFIXES) + tag
    return tag


def _maybe_suffix_digits(tag: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., TRACK1, TITLE2
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        return f"{tag}{rng.randint(1, 12)}"
    return tag


def _bounded_null_terminated(s: str, cap: int = 128) -> bytes:
    # Fuzzer trims to 128 then appends NUL; we ensure within cap and add NUL here too
    bs = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')[:cap]
    return bs + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strategy = rng.random()

    if strategy < 0.45:
        # Choose a common tag with case variants and optional prefix/suffix
        tag = rng.choice(COMMON_TAGS)
        tag = _case_variants(tag, rng)
        tag = _maybe_suffix_digits(tag, rng)
        tag = _maybe_prefix(tag, rng)
    elif strategy < 0.75:
        # Construct extended but valid custom tag
        tag = _random_extended_tag(rng)
        tag = _maybe_prefix(tag, rng)
    else:
        # Compose multi-part tag with separators to test parsing behavior
        parts = []
        n = rng.randint(2, 4)
        for _ in range(n):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(rng.choice(COMMON_TAGS))
            else:
                parts.append(_random_extended_tag(rng, max_len=16))
        sep = rng.choice(['_', '-', '.'])
        tag = sep.join(_case_variants(p, rng) for p in parts)
        tag = _maybe_prefix(tag, rng)
        tag = _maybe_suffix_digits(tag, rng)

    # Ensure non-empty and within size, then NUL-terminate
    if not tag:
        tag = "TITLE"

    return _bounded_null_terminated(tag)

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces bytes for a single Ogg/Vorbis packet (ogg_packet.packet).
# It focuses on generating valid-looking Vorbis packets covering:
# - Identification header (mandatory first header)
# - Comment header (second header) with vendor and a few comments
# - Setup header (third header) – we emit a minimally structured placeholder; true
#   validity is complex but we keep it plausible-length and header-type correct.
# - Audio packets (mode bits + dummy payload), sized to be reasonable.
# The fuzzer stubs cap packet size at 2048 bytes; we stay under that limit.
# The output is a single packet; fuzzer drivers will set other ogg_packet fields.

VORBIS_MAGIC = b"vorbis"


def _u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<B", x & 0xFF)


def _u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<H", x & 0xFFFF)


def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<Q", x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pick(rng: random.Random, items: List):
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


# Vorbis requires first byte: packet_type (1,3,5 for headers) then "vorbis"
# Identification header layout (per spec):
#  - packet_type = 1
#  - "vorbis"
#  - version (u32 LE) = 0
#  - channels (u8) >=1
#  - sample_rate (u32 LE) >0
#  - bitrate_maximum (s32 LE) or nominal hints (we emit plausible values)
#  - bitrate_nominal (s32 LE)
#  - bitrate_minimum (s32 LE)
#  - blocksize (u8): 4 bits for short exp, 4 bits for long exp; valid exponents 0..13, long>=short
#  - framing flag (u8) bit0=1

def make_ident_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version = 0
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2, 6])
    rate = _pick(rng, [8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    # Choose bitrates around common values; -1 means unspecified
    nominal = _pick(rng, [64000, 96000, 128000, 160000, 192000, -1])
    if nominal == -1:
        bmin = -1
        bmax = -1
    else:
        # pick a window of +-64k around nominal ensuring min<=nominal<=max
        spread = _pick(rng, [32000, 64000, 96000])
        bmin = max(16000, nominal - spread)
        bmax = nominal + spread
    # blocksize exponents (powers of two). Ensure long >= short.
    short_exp = rng.choice([6, 7, 8])       # 64,128,256
    long_exp = rng.choice([8, 9, 10])       # 256,512,1024
    if long_exp < short_exp:
        long_exp = short_exp
    blocksize_byte = ((long_exp & 0x0F) << 4) | (short_exp & 0x0F)
    framing = 1  # must have bit0 set
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _u8(1)
    buf += VORBIS_MAGIC
    buf += _u32(version)
    buf += _u8(channels)
    buf += _u32(rate)
    # signed 32-bit for bitrates
    buf += struct.pack("<i", bmax)
    buf += struct.pack("<i", nominal)
    buf += struct.pack("<i", bmin)
    buf += _u8(blocksize_byte)
    buf += _u8(framing)
    return bytes(buf)


# Comment header layout:
#  - packet_type = 3
#  - "vorbis"
#  - vendor_length u32, vendor string (UTF-8)
#  - user_comment_list_length u32
#  - repeated: comment_length u32 + comment bytes
#  - framing bit u8 with bit0=1

def _utf8_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'strict')


def make_comment_header(rng: random.Random, max_size: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    vendor = _pick(rng, [
        "Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20101101",
        "AO; enc=libvorbis-1.3.x",
        "PythonVorbisGen 1.0",
    ])
    comments_pool = [
        "TITLE=Test Tone",
        "ARTIST=Fuzzer",
        "ALBUM=Corpus",
        "DATE=2025",
        "TRACKNUMBER=1",
        "COMMENT=Generated by seed"
    ]
    # Choose 0..5 comments
    ncomments = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    chosen = rng.sample(comments_pool, k=ncomments) if ncomments else []
    # Optionally add some randomized tags
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(chosen) < 6:
        tag = f"ENCODER_OPTIONS=-q{rng.choice([2,4,6,8])}"
        chosen.append(tag)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _u8(3)
    buf += VORBIS_MAGIC
    vbytes = _utf8_bytes(vendor)
    buf += _u32(len(vbytes))
    buf += vbytes
    buf += _u32(len(chosen))
    for c in chosen:
        cbytes = _utf8_bytes(c)
        buf += _u32(len(cbytes))
        buf += cbytes
        if len(buf) > max_size - 1:
            break
    buf += _u8(1)  # framing bit
    # Ensure size cap
    return bytes(buf[:max_size])


# Setup header is highly complex; we only emit the correct header type and
# a plausible payload length to pass cursory header parsing paths.
#  - packet_type = 5
#  - "vorbis"
#  - payload: arbitrary bytes. We'll keep a small, random size.

def make_setup_header(rng: random.Random, max_size: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _u8(5)
    buf += VORBIS_MAGIC
    # Include some structured-looking bytes to vary code paths
    payload_len = rng.randrange(32, min(512, max_size - len(buf)))
    # Start with a few mode/codebook-ish markers
    prefix = bytes([
        rng.randrange(0, 2),                # codebook marker bit-ish
        rng.randrange(0, 2),                # time domain transforms flag
        rng.randrange(0, 4),                # floor count small
        rng.randrange(0, 4),                # residue count small
        rng.randrange(0, 2),                # mapping count small
        rng.randrange(0, 4),                # mode count small
    ])
    buf += prefix
    buf += _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, payload_len - len(prefix)))
    return bytes(buf[:max_size])


# Audio packet: begins with mode number bits LSB-first in the bitstream.
# We cannot pack bit-level here, but libraries often accept arbitrary payloads
# post-configuration. We'll supply a small to medium payload of random bytes.

def make_audio_packet(rng: random.Random, max_size: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    # To simulate a small header byte with low mode numbers
    first = rng.randrange(0, 16)  # lower modes
    size = rng.randrange(32, min(1024, max_size))
    payload = _u8(first) + _rand_bytes(rng, size - 1)
    return payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Weight toward producing a valid header sequence across fuzz runs.
    # For a single call, pick one of: id, comment, setup, or audio.
    kind = rng.choices(
        population=["id", "comment", "setup", "audio"],
        weights=[35, 30, 15, 20],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if kind == "id":
        pkt = make_ident_header(rng)
    elif kind == "comment":
        pkt = make_comment_header(rng)
    elif kind == "setup":
        pkt = make_setup_header(rng)
    else:
        pkt = make_audio_packet(rng)

    # Ensure not exceeding the fuzzer cap (2048) and overall constraint (<4096)
    return pkt[:2048]
